D017-D005_h022.question:
I’ve always cared about looking put together—being a social worker, I’m in front of people all the time, and I want to be professional, you know? But lately... it’s like I can’t stop seeing these flaws in my skin. There’s this tiny scar near my eyebrow—from a childhood fall, really faint—but in the mirror, it looks deep, ruined. I’ve had several peels, even a minor laser treatment last year. It’s not vanity. I *know* the marks are there, even if others don’t seem to notice. Sometimes I wonder—do they just not want to say anything?

I spend a lot of time in the morning making sure my foundation covers everything. If I skip it, I feel—exposed. Unfit. Like I shouldn’t be helping people if I can’t even manage myself.  

There are moments—rare—when I’ve felt like someone was commenting on my face when they weren’t speaking at all. Or that mirrors are... not lying, exactly, but *showing more truth* than people are willing to admit. I don’t think I’m losing touch with reality, but I can’t shake the feeling that I see things others don’t. It’s just... my skin, mostly. Always my skin. This has been building for about a year—not every second, but it’s there, like background noise.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D017-D005_h023.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now, mostly with how I look—specifically my nose. It feels… wrong. Too wide, lopsided, like it’s pushing everything else out of balance. I know people say it looks normal, but I can’t shake the feeling that it’s deformed. I used to glance in the mirror just to fix my tie or hair, but now I either can’t leave it alone—checking at every reflective surface, even truck windows—or I’ll avoid them completely, afraid of what I’ll see.  

It’s affecting work. I manage a warehouse, used to walk the floor all day, but now I find excuses to stay in the office. Don’t want the guys looking at me too long. Sometimes I catch myself wondering if they’re talking about my face behind my back—or if they’re even *real*, like, truly real, or just playing roles. I don’t hear voices or anything, but there’s this nagging sense that things aren’t as solid as they seem.  

My wife says I’m different—distant, obsessed. But she doesn’t see what I see. I don’t know if it’s in my head or if something’s changed in the world, but it feels real. I can’t tell if I’m losing it or if I’m the only one seeing clearly.

    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
